key_insight: DLite makes speculative decoding work better for agentic AI by removing dependence on stale history, which can badly hurt draft acceptance in long, multi-turn interactions. In simple terms, it redesigns drafting so the model stays efficient even as context keeps changing.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the drop in speculative decoding quality for agentic workloads, where long evolving contexts and repeated interactions can reduce draft acceptance length by up to 80% while still carrying historical KV cache overhead.
method: Designs a history-free speculative decoding strategy for agentic settings instead of relying on accumulated past draft history.
Targets the mismatch between long-context agent behavior and traditional draft models that become less accurate as interactions continue.
Improves inference efficiency by keeping candidate generation aligned with the current context rather than stale cached state.
impact: This matters because agentic AI systems often run many sequential tool calls and conversations, making inference speed critical. DLite can help practitioners keep latency lower and throughput higher without sacrificing the benefits of speculative decoding.

paper_title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
paper_authors: Jiaming Xu, Hanzhen Wang, Tianlang Zhao, Jiewen Xiao, Chengze Yuan
